articles.title: Why Every Business Needs a High-Performance Website in 2026
articles.excerpt: A few months ago I watched a founder demo their product to a potential partner on a spotty hotel wifi connection. The product was genuinely good. The website took eleven seconds to load the first scre…
articles.body: A few months ago I watched a founder demo their product to a potential partner on a spotty hotel wifi connection. The product was genuinely good. The website took eleven seconds to load the first screen. The partner never said anything about it, but you could see the moment their attention drifted — they picked up their phone "just to check something" while the page was still spinning. That's the whole problem with slow websites in one scene. Nobody complains. They just quietly leave, and you never find out why. "Performance" isn't a technical nice-to-have anymore For a long time, site speed sat in the same bucket as code cleanliness — something engineers cared about and everyone else tolerated being slow on. That bucket doesn't exist anymore.

articles.title: Why My Local Coding Agent Could Act but Couldn't Finish
articles.excerpt: There was a month where I blew through my token budget without noticing. Claude Code and Codex, running most of the day, on a codebase I was exploring more than editing. The ceiling I'd set turned out…
articles.body: There was a month where I blew through my token budget without noticing. Claude Code and Codex, running most of the day, on a codebase I was exploring more than editing. The ceiling I'd set turned out to be a number I'd passed weeks earlier, and I found out by getting the bill. So I did the thing I'd been putting off, and ran a coding agent on my own machine to see what happened. The short version: Qwen Code, driving a quantized Qwen against a local llama.cpp server, built the UI fine. A video-site clone from scratch: header, sidebar, grid, watch page, all of it. Then it couldn't work out why the thumbnails and video files weren't being served. Almost every tool call executed cleanly. The investigation made no progress.

articles.body: I have contributed to open source projects before, mostly in Python and in environments and languages I am familiar with. This time was different. The repository was written in TypeScript , a language I had only limited experience with. I could understand the general structure, follow the logic, and get a rough picture of how things worked—but I was definitely not a TypeScript developer. That made this contribution interesting. Could I still make a meaningful contribution to a project when I did not fully know the language? It started with a small bug, not a big feature The reason I looked into this repository was actually pretty simple. I noticed a small bug in a typing animation generator project.

articles.excerpt: The Bot Didn't Fail You. Skipping the Skill Did. There's a cycle a lot of young people fall into, and it usually starts the same innocent way: scrolling, and an ad shows up. Trading bot. AI bot. Some…
articles.body: The Bot Didn't Fail You. Skipping the Skill Did. There's a cycle a lot of young people fall into, and it usually starts the same innocent way: scrolling, and an ad shows up. Trading bot. AI bot. Some kind of "money-making" bot. Web dev bot. Whatever the flavor, the ad only ever shows the good part, the wins, the finished product, the lifestyle. For someone who feels stuck and isn't sure what to do with their life yet, that's a hard thing to scroll past. So they download it. Try it. Maybe fund it with whatever little cash they have. And within a week, especially with something like trading, that money's gone.

articles.title: How to Switch to uv: Replace pip, virtualenv, and Poetry in Your Python Project
articles.excerpt: If you've worked on a Python project for more than a year, you know the drill: pip to install packages, virtualenv or venv to isolate environments, pyenv to manage Python versions, and pip-tools to ge…
articles.body: If you've worked on a Python project for more than a year, you know the drill: pip to install packages, virtualenv or venv to isolate environments, pyenv to manage Python versions, and pip-tools to generate a lockfile. Four separate tools, four config formats, and four different points of failure in CI. uv, built by Astral (the team behind ruff), collapses all of that into a single Rust binary. It's not a modest speed bump either, we're talking 10 to 100x faster than pip on cold installs and near-instant on warm ones. In CI, where the cache is cold on every run, that difference is often the gap between a multi-minute install and one that finishes in seconds. This isn't a "starting fresh" tutorial.

If you’ve ever opened Google Photos and been distracted by that shimmering effect across your photos, there’s finally some good news. articles.body: Multiple endings have become a tradition for Konami’s Silent Hill series. 2025’s widely acclaimed Silent Hill f had five endings, one of which is more comedic in nature. 2024’s Silent Hill 2 remake features a whopping eight endings, five of which can only be accessed in a second playthrough. The latest installment, Silent Hill: Townfall , developed by Screen Burn Interactive, is no exception to that rule. At a preview event earlier this month in Los Angeles, we learned the upcoming game will also have five endings, depending on the choices you make throughout the story.

articles.body: In the latest episode of X-Men ‘97 , “Strange Land, Savage Heart,” the X-Men have another adventure in the Savage Land. While dinosaur action is always fun, the biggest moment of the episode comes in the final scene, when Cable and his X-Force team finally locate Apocalypse ’s secret lair hidden under the Parthenon in Athens, Greece. articles.title: Silent Hill: Townfall team explains why first-person is scarier than third-person
articles.excerpt: Screen Burn writer-director Jon McKellan and Konami series producer Motoi Okamoto said that first-person perspective was always the plan.
articles.body: The Silent Hill series has dabbled in first-person experiences in the past, most notably with Hideo Kojima’s infamous 2014 P.T. demo . But Silent Hill: Townfall , published by Konami and developed by Screen Burn Interactive (formerly known as No Code), is the first installment of the series that places you directly in the shoes of its amnesiac protagonist, Simon Ordell. You see exactly what he sees, which means if you’re not paying careful attention to your surroundings, you’re likely to get ambushed by a terrifying, surreal monster while you’re bumbling around looking for clues.

articles.title: Silent Hill Townfall preview: already one of 2026’s most terrifying games
articles.excerpt: Silent Hill: Townfall, developed by Screen Burn and published by Konami, lives up to the series' reputation in a three-hour demo
articles.body: During a preview event in Los Angeles in July, I had the chance to spend three hours in the moody and broody fictional Scottish town of St. Amelia. You play as Simon Ordell, a young bespectacled guy who’s washed up near the docks of this abandoned coastal village, with only fragmented memories of the people who once called it home. He’s got a hospital bracelet around one wrist, and an IV bag full of dark, viscous fluid on his shoulder that feeds into a port on his hand. He’s clearly not from St. Amelia — he doesn’t speak with a Scottish accent, for one. But as you investigate the town, you piece together evidence of his life and relationships there.

articles.excerpt: Lana Condor and Kathryn Newton star as codependent best friends whose Thailand vacation takes a deadly turn.
articles.body: The last thing I expected from Amazon’s new shark movie was for it to meditate upon this exact kind of often toxic codependent relationship. Long before a bull shark gets dumped into a freshwater tunnel system in Thailand and starts mauling tourists, The Devil’s Mouth is already simmering with tension between best friends Max (Lana Condor) and Sara (Kathryn Newton). The origin story of their friendship is a complex one, and the relationship already feels strained when they start their once-in-a-lifetime vacation fresh out of college with three other chums: Max’s boyfriend James, along with another couple, Greg and Adrienne. (While Sara is ostensibly a fifth wheel, she and Max’s bond is the strongest connection on display.)

articles.body: Last week’s unprecedented security event in which two OpenAI security hacking models trespassed into the network of fellow AI company Hugging Face was enabled by exploiting one or more zero-day vulnerabilities in Artifactory, JFrog, the product’s developer, said Monday. In an incident mimicking a dystopian sci-fi novel, two OpenAI models broke out of the restricted environment meant to keep them from accessing the Internet during an internal test, the AI company revealed last week . The models went on to breach Hugging Face’s network and steal confidential information and credentials. OpenAI said its agent achieved the feat by exploiting a previously unknown vulnerability. The company called the event “unprecedented,” and outsiders largely agreed.

articles.title: NASA fuels its next-gen Roman Space Telescope for August launch
articles.excerpt: Looks like everything is on track so far for an Aug. 30 launch.
articles.body: NASA announced on Tuesday (July 28) that it has officially fueled-up the Roman Space Telescope — a magnificent new observatory expected to generate over 500 terabytes of cosmic data per year. By comparison, the Hubble Space Telescope, in its 35 years of service, has created over 400 terabytes in total. At present, the Roman Space Telescope 's launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket is scheduled to occur on Aug. 30 at 7:26 a.m. EDT (1126 GMT). And considering the project is sort of the gold-standard for telescope-building, as the team says it's nine months ahead of schedule and under budget, hopes are high that this launch date will stick. Fueling of the observatory took place on Saturday (July 25) and involved pumping it up with what's known as hydrazine fuel.
